decisions: D28 Round 4 'Fixtures and assignment' (catalogue rule); P5 decisions 16 Nov 2026: pre-P3 candidate superset, per-range fixtures, vendor pages with CNA fallback (status 'unaffected' entries only), stable releases only, SHA-256 of evidence files, Windows vulnerable build = prior MSRC FixedBuild; eligible view from frozen effect labels p3-labels-v2.1 (P5 decision 16 Nov 2026)
windows_update_history_note: P5w (Devansh 16 Nov 2026): Windows Server 2012 R2, 2016, 2019 and 2022 take dated build fixtures from Microsoft's official per-version update-history pages; per CVE the fixing KB MSRC lists for the product maps to its release (fixed fixture), and the release before it in the history is the vulnerable fixture. Supersedes OQ-P5-4 (prior MSRC FixedBuild) and Round 4 'No full build histories' for these four versions. The 2016/2019/2022 pages give each KB's OS build (version 10.0.<build>); the 2012 R2 page gives none, so its releases are the cumulative monthly rollups identified by KB. Exchange and SQL Server keep the P5 rule.
windows_update_history_followup_note: P5w follow-up (Devansh 17 Nov 2026): fixing KBs missing from the history page are read from their official support articles (cumulative: a release; else a standalone KB on the latest earlier release); optional non-security previews (label Preview, or update type C/D in the release information) are not releases, out-of-band updates are; each version starts with its initial release: the release information A row (2016, 2019), else the lifecycle GA date with the build line (2022: 10.0.20348; the release information gives no initial 2022 build) or RTM (2012 R2, not on the release information page).

Start Date Mainstream End Date Extended End Date Windows Server 2022 (?P<date>\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{4})

unverified_release.decision: Devansh 16 Nov 2026 (BUILD_RULES rule 13): for CVEs with no verified fixture (wording confirmed per CVE, OQ-P5v-1, Devansh 16 Nov 2026; first written 'for products with no fixtures'), vulnerable fixtures from exact version strings listed in NVD CPE matches, flagged unverified_release: no release date, no upstream validation, vulnerable fixtures only, never a fixed fixture; usable in the primary (p = 1) benchmark, not in p<1 cohorts; only strings NVD itself lists; OQ-P5-11 (Devansh 16 Nov 2026, rule 13): inclusive range endpoints (versionStartIncluding, versionEndIncluding) also accepted, exclusive never; one fixture per CVE, the highest such version (OQ-P5-12)

p5v: P5v 16 Nov 2026: the unverified_release products verified against vendor release evidence. oracle:mysql, mysql:mysql, solarwinds:serv-u and postfix:postfix moved from not_covered to products (dated vendor release lists found); cerberusftp:ftp_server release patterns extended to the page's older date formats; crushftp:crushftp stays not covered. Per CVE, a verified vulnerable fixture replaces the unverified one; CVEs without one keep their unverified_release fixture (task P5v).
p5v_followup: P5v follow-up, decided 16 Nov 2026 by Devansh: OQ-P5v-1 per-CVE unverified rule confirmed; OQ-P5v-2 an official vendor version list counts as release evidence without dates, date recorded 'undated' (crushftp:crushftp moved from not_covered to products); OQ-P5v-3 a hotfix an official vendor advisory names as the fix counts as the fixed release, citing that advisory (Serv-U).

mysql:mysql.releases_note: MySQL release notes, one index per series; the GA pattern keeps only dated entries without a pre-release label (Milestone, Development Milestone, Release Candidate, Not released, Not yet released are excluded). The 8.4 index also lists the 8.1-8.3 innovation releases, the 9.7 index the 9.0-9.6 ones. The 5.5 and 5.6 indexes are no longer served by dev.mysql.com (redirect, probe 16 Nov 2026) and are read from Wayback Machine captures of the vendor page.
mysql:mysql.evidence_note: no vendor fix document names these CVEs: the MySQL release notes sampled (5.7.14, 5.7.15, 5.7.44, 8.0.12, 8.0.36) carry no CVE IDs, Oracle Critical Patch Update advisories list affected versions only, and the Oracle CNA records give affected bounds only (P5); a bound alone is never a fix (OQ-P5-3)

postfix:postfix.releases_note: ftp.cs.uu.nl mirrors the official release directory (ftp.porcupine.org/mirrors/postfix-release/official/, 403 to this client); the mirror is listed on https://www.postfix.org/download.html (probe 16 Nov 2026)

evidence.urls_note: NVD's record of CVE-2017-10140 links this announcement with the tag Vendor Advisory; the announcement names no CVE ID, so the pattern also requires its DB_CONFIG security entry under Fixed in all supported releases
patterns: Postfix stable release (?P<v>\d+\.\d+\.\d+ and legacy releases [\d., and]+?) \[An on-line version of this announcement.{0,600}?Fixed in all supported releases: Security: Berkeley DB versions 2 and later try to read settings from a file DB_CONFIG

solarwinds:serv-u.releases_note: one vendor release-notes page per release (title and Release date line); 15.4.2 to 2026.3 from the live documentation site, 15.1 to 15.4.1 from Wayback Machine captures of the same vendor URLs (the live pages answer 404, P5 probe). Hotfixes are listed only where they have a release-notes page (15.5.4 Hotfix 1).

evidence.fix_releases_note: OQ-P5v-3 (Devansh 16 Nov 2026): a hotfix the advisory names as the fixed software release counts as the fixed release, dated 'undated', citing the advisory

crushftp:crushftp.releases_note: OQ-P5v-2 (Devansh 16 Nov 2026): the vendor version pages are an official version list; a release they name without a date is recorded 'undated'. Names come from version header lines, lines that open with a version (also after a build prefix '_N:', e.g. '_24:10.5.3:'), the second half of '10.6.1 / 10.7.1:', and, on the 7.x and 8.x pages, dated lines 'CrushFTP 8.1.0 - 04/11/2017' (month first). Major versions 7 to 11 only, so library versions (OpenSSL, Java) never match. Builds (_N) are not releases: NVD versions are X.Y.Z.
crushftp:crushftp.evidence_note: fix statements: the version pages (a CVE inside a version section is fixed in that version) and the v10 and v11 wiki Update pages, which NVD links as Vendor Advisory for CrushFTP CVEs; a 'versions below X are vulnerable' sentence alone is a bound, not a fix (OQ-P5-3)

cerberusftp:ftp_server.releases_note: one page, three date formats (P5v: P5 read only the first, so releases before 2025 were missed): '22 September 2026', 'March 25 2025', and month/day/year ('2/09/2017'; month first: 8.0.12.1 is 8/1/2017 and 8.0.11 is 3/17/2017). BETA entries never match.

evidence.pattern: Samba (?:versions? )?(?P<v>\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:(?:,| and|,? and) \d+\.\d+\.\d+)*) (?:has|have) been issued as (?:a )?security releases?

mariadb:mariadb.evidence_note: no vendor fix page reachable: mariadb.com/kb/en/security/ redirects to a docs page that answered 404, mariadb.org/about/security/ redirects to an unrelated page (probe 16 Nov 2026); the Oracle CNA records for these CVEs are not the vendor's

cna_tarball.org_id_note: the orgId every published record in the kernel CNA's vulns repository carries (checked at build); the repository is the vendor's own
